intended_object: An internal helper in the library's Navier–Stokes development. It takes the azimuthal vector potential built from a stream function Ψ on a scaled graph chart and maps it through a local polar chart, giving a Cartesian velocity field. This is inferred from the docstring ("the same local polar realization used by the physical cycle prefixes") and the module documentation.
explanation: The body just composes two of the library's own constructions: `CyclePhysicalPrefixes.polarVelocityMap a j` applied to `componentPotential G Ψ`. Here `componentPotential` packs the rescaled stream potential `(velocityScale/radialScale) * Ψ(chartPoint G z)` into its azimuthal slot. Its inputs are library-specific data: a `ScaledGraph`, a polar chart index and a parameter `a`. Its docstring only says it reuses the realization from another file. Nothing in the literature is defined this way; it is bookkeeping inside a proof-specific chain of constructions, used to state that the Cartesian curl of the mean potential gives the meridional stream pair. So it has no standard mathematical counterpart to compare against.
